value.question: Can computed capsid–receptor structures and pH-resolved MD contact lifetimes classify which AAV capsids cross brain endothelium versus stay inside cells?
value.hypothesis: Epitope geometry from AlphaFold plus pH contact survival from many short replicas separates transcytosing LRP6/ALPL binders from retained capsids [s_lrp6][s_moyer].

compute_axis.quantity: independent 10-ns MD replicas per (peptide, receptor, pH) condition

held_fixed: six capsid peptides and four receptor domain sequences at every level
same pH 7.4 and 5.5 protonation sets, prepared once
same solvated boxes near 80,000 atoms, 2-fs step, 300 K, 150 mM NaCl
same AlphaFold-Multimer models, seeded once; replicas differ only in MD velocity seeds
same score: epitope contacts, buried area, pH contact-survival ratio

predictions.if_lever: At 32 ten-ns replicas per condition the score reaches AUC ≥ 0.9 and pH ratio > 2, matching the 320-ns run [s_moyer].
predictions.if_not: At 8–32 replicas the score stays at AUC ≤ 0.75 with no pH difference; the 320-ns run agrees, so more replicas do not help.
predictions.decision_rule: If at 32 replicas AUC over the six labelled pairs is ≥ 0.90 and the ALPL–VCAP-102 pH survival ratio exceeds 2.0, call if_lever; if AUC ≤ 0.75 at 8, 16 and 32, call if_not; between those, unsure.
predictions.noise_rule: Two disjoint 16-replica halves give split-half AUCs; a difference is real only if both halves clear the threshold and differ by less than 0.10 AUC; velocity seeds are independent per replica.
predictions.expected_why: AlphaFold already separates binders from non-binders [s_lrp6], but ten-ns contact survival may be too short to recover the measured pH-5.5 release [s_moyer].

value.compute_tested_why: The test varies independent replicas per condition, exactly the quantity parallel GPU compute buys; 8, 16 and 32 are nested subsets of one 384-replica run.
value.scored_against: Published labels: LRP6-dependent BBB potency of AAV9-X1.1 and CAP-Mac versus AAV9 [s_lrp6_pbmec], the E1-not-E3E4 domain assignment [s_lrp6_spr], and the measured ALPL–VCAP-102 pH release [s_moyer].

arms.what: ColabFold AlphaFold-Multimer on 24 peptide–domain complexes, 5 models each, up to 20 recycles [s_lrp6].
GROMACS: 32 independent 10-ns replicas per pair at pH 7.4 and 5.5, one replica per V100 GPU.
Sequential anchors: one 320-ns trajectory per anchored condition on one V100, same settings.
Score epitope geometry and pH contact survival at N = 8, 16, 32 and compare with published outcomes.

baseline.what: One long 320-ns GROMACS trajectory per condition on one V100, the strongest sequential sampling the same aggregate simulated time buys.

anchor.what: Reproduce the published AlphaFold-Multimer finding that X1 and CAP-Mac peptides bind LRP6 E1, not E3E4 [s_lrp6].
anchor.published_value: E1 preferred over E3E4 for both X1 and CAP-Mac peptides
anchor.tolerance: top-ranked of 5 models docks E1 not E3E4 for both peptides, at least 4 of 5 models agree
anchor.independent_code: ColabFold batch with AlphaFold-Multimer v2 weights (public repository)

checks: pilot-measured ns/day within a factor 2 of the Kutzner-derived proxy before the main spend
contact autocorrelation time ≤ 2 ns in pilot replicas, else fewer longer replicas
pH 5.5 and 7.4 systems differ only in protonation of His, Glu and Asp
ensemble contact occupancy within ±0.15 of the 320-ns sequential trajectory
split-half AUCs differ by less than 0.10
every number used in cost or test size carries a basis and, if proxied, its phase

phases.stop_rule: 4-hour timer on the 8xA100 instance, or all 24 complexes finished.

gate.else: stop and report that the pipeline cannot reproduce the published epitope assignment; no MD spend.

phases.what: Two 10-ns replicas on two V100s for ALPL–VCAP-102 at both pH values; measure ns/day and contact autocorrelation tau.
phases.stop_rule: 2-hour timer; also stop and rescale if ns/day falls below the md gate floor.

gate.else: switch to 8 replicas of 40 ns per condition and 6 conditions, then recompute cost.

phases.what: Run 384 ten-ns replicas (32 per condition over 12 conditions) across 8 V100 GPUs.
phases.stop_rule: 80-hour timer; if at 60 h fewer than half the replicas are done, continue at 16 replicas per condition.

gate.else: set n_replicas_max to 16 and take the short baseline instead of full sequential anchors.

phases.what: Time both baselines: 8 sequential 320-ns trajectories (one per anchored condition) on the 8 V100s, plus the side-by-side copies timing.
Assemble the score at N = 8, 16, 32; split-half noise; compare with published labels and the pH pair; write the report.

restructuring.sequential_part: One trajectory's 10^9–10^12 ordered 2-fs steps, each frame waiting on the last [s_jones].
restructuring.method: Many short independent replicas run at once; contacts decorrelate inside each replica, so weak scaling beats one long run [s_kasson][s_kutzner_ens].
restructuring.condition: Contacts must break and reform within a replica (tau ≤ 2 ns) so replicas decorrelate; measured as contact autocorrelation in pilot replicas.
restructuring.baseline_sequential: One 320-ns GROMACS run on one V100, GPU-resident PME, update and bonded offload, 2 fs, h-bonds constrained, one rank with 8 OpenMP threads.
restructuring.baseline_copies: 32 independent 10-ns copies started together on the same V100 GPUs, timed with and without reseeding.

scope_gap: Full glycosylated 60-mer capsids in water or membrane; here only peptide–domain fragments
True millisecond-scale pH-resolved off-rates; here only 10-ns contact-survival proxies
Hundreds of variants and many receptors; here 24 complex models and 12 MD conditions
Cell-level transcytosis versus retention in endothelium; here only published labels

novelty.closest_prior: Adaptive-sampling Markov models matched one long villin run with up to 5,000 parallel simulations per iteration [s_bowman]; capsid work used 5 AlphaFold models per peptide [s_lrp6].
novelty.left_open: Whether computed pH-resolved contact lifetimes classify transcytosis versus retention at all; only one pair has measured pH kinetics [s_moyer].

limits: Ten-ns contact-survival proxies, not millisecond off-rates.
Peptide–domain fragments in water, not full glycosylated capsids.
Six pairs, no cell-level transcytosis measured.
value.test_summary: ColabFold AlphaFold-Multimer on 24 peptide–receptor complexes, then 32 ten-ns GROMACS replicas per pair at pH 7.4 and 5.5 on 8 V100s; compared with 320-ns sequential runs and published binding, domain and pH-release results [s_lrp6][s_moyer].

items.page_quote: We identify LRP6 as a previously-unreported and highly-conserved target for BBB transcytosis by AAV9-X1.1 (PMC11381518); We identify alkaline phosphatase (ALPL) as the primary receptor used by VCAP-102 to cross the BBB and demonstrate that direct binding of VCAP-102 to human ALPL can initiate receptor-mediated transcytosis in a cell barrier model (bioRxiv 2024.03.12.584703 abstract)
items.note: This is the plan's research question about what it will compute and measure, not a factual claim, so it needs no source. Its premises (AAV capsids crossing brain endothelium via LRP6/ALPL; pH-dependent capsid-receptor release) are on the cited literature pages.

items.page_quote: Representative AlphaFold models, from 5 structural models each of X1 and CAP-Mac peptides with up to 20 recycles, predict selective interaction with human LRP6 domain E1 (E1 and E2: teal, E3 and E4: yellow, AAV peptides: purple). / We observed direct capsid-receptor interaction in a cell-free assay using Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) analysis with recombinant ALPL, showing that VCAP-102 directly interacts with ALPL with an affinity (KD) of ∼20nm at pH7.4 (Fig. 4c). Rapid dissociation of the ALPL-VCAP-102 complex was observed at pH 5.5.
items.note: Both recorded quotes appear verbatim on their pages (PMC11381518 Fig. 4c legend; bioRxiv 2024.03.12.584703 PDF text retrieved via search index after direct fetch returned 429). They support the AlphaFold epitope-geometry precedent and the measured pH-dependent dissociation of one capsid-receptor pair. The claim that these features separate transcytosing from retained capsids is the plan's hypothesis/prediction and needs no source; the pages' transcytosis framing ('LRP6 as blood-brain barrier transcytosis receptor'; 'ALPL is the primary receptor used by VCAP-102 to cross the BBB') is consistent with it.

items.page_quote: Time steps that are chosen for simulations are typically on the order of femtoseconds (10–15s) for reasons concerning numerical stability and simulation quality... The number of sequential operations needed to achieve these time scales can grow to be at least 10^9–10^12.
items.note: Quote appears verbatim on PMC9281402 and supports the 10^9–10^12 sequential, ordered integration steps of one trajectory. The 2-fs step is the plan's own integration setting and falls within the page's 'on the order of femtoseconds' statement.

items.page_quote: In a system with multiple metastable states and good separation of timescales, individual trajectories will decorrelate within a metastable state much faster than they transition between states. / ...most compute platforms have better weak scaling than strong scaling (one could double the system "size" or in this case run 2 systems and get better performance than running the original system with twice as many compute elements). / problems that previously required the generation of a few long trajectories are nowadays often addressed by ensemble methods that instead need a large number of shorter trajectories.
items.note: Both recorded quotes appear verbatim (PMC9476681; arXiv:1903.05918v1). The Kasson page additionally states the weak-scaling argument for ensembles, supporting 'weak scaling beats one long run'; the Kutzner page supports many short trajectories replacing a few long ones.

items.page_quote: We observed direct capsid-receptor interaction in a cell-free assay using Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) analysis with recombinant ALPL, showing that VCAP-102 directly interacts with ALPL with an affinity (KD) of ∼20nm at pH7.4 (Fig. 4c). Rapid dissociation of the ALPL-VCAP-102 complex was observed at pH 5.5.
items.note: Quote appears on the bioRxiv preprint and supports the pH-resolved release behavior of the measured pair. The lever thresholds (32 x 10-ns replicas, AUC >= 0.9, pH ratio > 2, agreement with the 320-ns run) are the plan's predicted outcome under the lever, not claims about published results, so they need no source; the page states no such values.

items.page_quote: We observed direct capsid-receptor interaction in a cell-free assay using Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) analysis with recombinant ALPL, showing that VCAP-102 directly interacts with ALPL with an affinity (KD) of ∼20nm at pH7.4 (Fig. 4c).
